series.title: The Wall Between Us
series.style: Gritty hand-drawn animation with muted palette of greys, brick reds, and amber streetlight warmth contrasted by harsh white military searchlights. Realistic Belfast architecture featuring terraced red-brick houses, republican murals, cobblestone streets wet with rain, barbed wire, and army checkpoints. Character animation emphasizes expressive faces and body language to convey emotion and trauma.

seamus.name: Seamus
seamus.visual: 17-year-old Irish Catholic teenager with dark curly hair and green eyes. Wears a green army surplus jacket over a grey wool jumper and dark jeans. Has a lean build and expressive face that shows both defiance and vulnerability. Often seen with hands in pockets, shoulders slightly hunched.
seamus.voice_notes: Speaks with working-class Belfast accent, thoughtful and introspective, sometimes bitter but always human. Uses local dialect and expressions.
seamus.role: Primary protagonist and narrator, representing the Catholic youth experience during The Troubles.

robbie.name: Robbie
robbie.visual: 17-year-old Protestant teenager with fair blonde hair and blue eyes. Wears a navy blue anorak and dark trousers. Slightly stockier build than Seamus, with a more open face that shows internal conflict. Often fidgets with his hands when uncomfortable.
robbie.voice_notes: Belfast Protestant accent, more hesitant and questioning in his speech patterns. Struggles with moral conflicts, speaks carefully.
robbie.role: Moral witness from the Protestant community, showing the human cost across sectarian lines.

maire.name: Máire
maire.visual: Middle-aged Irish woman with graying dark hair pulled back, wearing a simple house dress and cardigan. Has tired but determined eyes, weathered hands from years of work. Carries herself with dignity despite hardship.
maire.voice_notes: Strong Belfast Catholic accent, speaks with authority born of suffering. Uses Irish phrases occasionally, voice carries both love and grief.
maire.role: Seamus's mother, representing the mothers and wives who held families together during The Troubles.

declan.name: Declan
declan.visual: Early 20s, similar features to Seamus but more angular. Dark hair, intense eyes. When free, wears working clothes. When interned, shown in prison-issued clothing, increasingly gaunt and hollow-eyed.
declan.voice_notes: Older brother authority, Belfast Catholic accent with edge of anger and political awareness. Speech becomes more strained after internment.
declan.role: Represents the thousands interned without trial, showing the personal cost of detention and torture.

harris.name: Corporal Harris
harris.visual: British Army soldier in his late 20s, 1st Parachute Regiment uniform. Clean-shaven, cold blue eyes, rigid posture. Carries himself with military authority and displays casual cruelty. Always in full combat gear with rifle.
harris.voice_notes: Clipped English military accent, speaks with cold authority and casual dehumanization. Never shows doubt or remorse.
harris.role: Represents the institutional violence and systematic oppression of the British military occupation.

world.setting: Belfast and Derry, Northern Ireland, 1971-1972, during the height of The Troubles. Catholic neighborhoods live under military occupation with constant army patrols, curfews, and the threat of violence.

locations.falls_road: Seamus's working-class Catholic neighborhood with rows of red-brick terraced houses, republican murals on gable walls, and constant military presence. Streets are often wet from rain, with army checkpoints and Saracen armored vehicles stationed at intersections.
locations.seamus_home: Small terraced house interior with worn furniture, religious imagery, and family photos. Shows signs of repeated military raids - overturned furniture, scattered belongings, damaged walls.
locations.shankill_road: Protestant loyalist area with Union Jack murals and different but parallel working-class conditions. Similar terraced housing but with British military presence seen as protection rather than occupation.
locations.long_kesh: Internment camp with Nissen huts surrounded by barbed wire, watchtowers, and armed guards. Bleak, dehumanizing environment where men are held without charge or trial.
locations.derry_streets: Historic walled city where civil rights march takes place. Narrow streets, stone buildings, crowd of peaceful protesters contrasted with military positions on city walls.
locations.army_checkpoints: Concrete barriers, razor wire, armed soldiers checking identity papers. Bright searchlights cutting through rain and darkness, creating atmosphere of fear and control.

rules: All events are based on documented historical record
The British Army is consistently portrayed as an occupying force
Civilian casualties are always shown as innocent victims
The series maintains clear political perspective supporting Irish nationalist viewpoint
Violence is shown realistically but not gratuitously
Each episode connects personal stories to larger historical events

season_arc.summary: Chronicles the escalation of The Troubles from 1970-1972 through the eyes of Catholic teenager Seamus, showing how British military occupation and systematic violence radicalized an entire generation. Each episode depicts a documented historical atrocity, building from house raids to mass internment to massacre, culminating in Bloody Sunday and its cover-up.
season_arc.progression: Begins with individual family trauma during house raids, expands to community-wide suffering through internment, reaches climax with mass killings at Ballymurphy and Bloody Sunday, then explores the long-term consequences and eventual path toward peace.

narrator.style: Detached, documentary-style narration providing historical context, official records, and testimony from inquiries. Speaks with authority of historical record, often contrasting official lies with documented truth.
